top_stories.title: How Yair Alon went from building Portrait Mode at Google to founding researcher at Poetiq
top_stories.content: Yair Alon spent a decade at Google Research and DeepMind. He built the deep learning models behind Portrait Mode on Pixel phones. He published papers on efficient deep learning. He designed models for Search, Ads, and YouTube. His last project was VideoPoet, a video generation system. Everything was great, by his own account. But he felt that small startups had become where the most exciting innovations were happening. So when former DeepMind collaborators told him they were starting a company, he knew immediately he wanted in.That company is Poetiq (YC S26, San Francisco). In one sentence: Poetiq is building an AI system that can optimize any other AI system, including itself.Leaving Google after a decadeYair had been at Google since his PhD internship at CMU, where he studied machine learning and computer vision. He knew how to be productive and successful inside that ecosystem. Leaving felt scary. "I was there for so many years," he says. "I knew how to be productive and successful in that environment so leaving felt like a scary new thing." items.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
items.content: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont. Both Beaumont and the CTO and co-founder of security firm Phorian said that version 2.1.313 was distributed through Anthropic’s official account on Cursor. So far, neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attackers gained control of the account. In search of cloud credentials “It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. Extensions auto-update in Cursor by default, but users can configure this in settings.” Phorian has more details here.Read full article Comments

items.content: dbreunig/nesformer Inspired by qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal, Drew Breunig baked a working emulator for a Nintendo Entertainment System 6502 CPU into the weights of Qwen3.5-4B. You can now play NES ROMs such as Super Mario Bros (very slowly) running inside Qwen! In a comment on Hacker News Drew reveals the Opus 5.5 prompts he used to build this system: Read this article and any relevant source code: https://divagr.com/blog/qwenputer. Then explore if you could emulate the chip and ram in a Nintendo Entertainment System (as people do today with FPGAs in MISTRs) using this technique. If so, what size model would you have to build and if you could use smaller faster ones, could you get it to be at the standard clockspeed. Followed by: I think we should build it! Just for fun. It's okay if it's not fast. We want to be able to have the weights, and a cli to run them that we can point at a ROM. Apparently Opus found and then used this collection of conformance tests for the NES CPU released 15 years ago by Christopher Pow. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space: Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. ✨ Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well.
